top_categories.workout_context: Viana Granfondo's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.

Road-specific control matters at Viana Granfondo. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 80 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Viana Granfondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
At mile 60 of 80, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Viana Granfondo. Train it until it feels boring.
At Viana Granfondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Viana Granfondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 80 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Viana Granfondo's mixed terrain actually does to you.
2-minute all-out efforts on mixed terrain. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 80 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

race_overlay.weather: March in Viana do Castelo, Alto Minho, Portugal — Mid-March in Alto Minho: cool, Atlantic-influenced, with a real chance of rain and wind off the coast. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Viana Granfondo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Viana Granfondo’s 80 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Viana Granfondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 80 miles of mixed terrain in Viana do Castelo, Alto Minho, Portugal.
